title: Regular pay above the published scale, by unit
question: How many payroll rows had regular pay well above 26 times the highest biweekly rate the Department of Human Resources publishes for the job code, by unit?
finding: In fiscal 2026, 545 rows were paid more than 10% and $10,000 above the top of their job code's scale, $18.6 million above it in all (fiscal 2019: 201 rows, $6.2 million). Most by amount: Firefighters,Local 798, Unit 1 (unit 798) 151 rows, $5.1 million; Prof & Tech Eng, Local 21 (unit 021) 82 rows, $5.1 million; POA (unit 911) 72 rows, $2.1 million. Largest job codes: Firefighter (job H002, Firefighters,Local 798, Unit 1): 54 rows, $1.6 million above a yearly top of $151,918; Transit Operator (job 9163, TWU, Local 250-A, TransitOpr): 103 rows, $1.5 million above a yearly top of $100,360; Lieutenant, Fire Suppression (job H020, Firefighters,Local 798, Unit 1): 39 rows, $1.3 million above a yearly top of $176,592.
how: Each row's salaries are set against 26 times the highest biweekly maximum the Department of Human Resources lists for that job code in that fiscal year (any set of rates, any effective date, so the January raise is already in and the test is generous to the employee). Fiscal 2026 uses the FY2025-26 hourly-rates workbook; earlier years use the same Department's table on DataSF. A row is counted when salaries exceed the top by more than 10% and by $10,000.
limits: The Controller's 'salaries' can hold retroactive pay for an earlier year, a 27th pay period, acting pay at a higher class, premiums some agreements fold into base pay, and pay for time in a second class under the same job code; uniformed ranks can carry rank premiums. A row is a question for the payroll office, not an overpayment.
